name: Eaveside terrace pair
role: Dense residential rows and varied roofs beyond the playable boundary
design: ONE JOINED TERRACE ASSET containing TWO attached ordinary homes on a shared flat street foundation, approximately 11 m combined frontage by 6.5 m deep. In the LEFT front-right view, the LEFT dwelling has THREE full storeys with warm cream plaster, a steep terracotta gable and a small attic window; the RIGHT dwelling has TWO storeys with pale ochre plaster and a lower deep-teal half-hipped roof. Their roof heights clearly STEP DOWN, forming an irregular domestic skyline. Each home has its own plain front door and modest shuttered domestic windows, both on the same street-facing facade; the party wall and gutter junction are structurally continuous. Two small chimney stacks, simple oak bands and modest repaired shutters, no shops. On the opposite BACK-LEFT view, the TALLER unit appears on VIEWER-RIGHT and the LOWER unit on VIEWER-LEFT, a real 180-degree rotation of this same pair. Show the previously hidden plain left end wall and both backs, with two kitchen doors, a small shared laundry recess and rain barrel. Do not repeat the street facade or merely mirror the first image. No whole street or extra third/fourth house; just this one useful joined two-home background cluster.
